VERIFIED BY THE CHIEF against source, not accepted on report. RecallUnit (recall/unit.scala) carries BOTH span: SpanSet AND text: String. RecallGraph.validated (graph.scala:34-48) checks exactly three things - duplicate ids, ordinals forming 0..n-1, and u.span.minSpan.endExclusive <= transcript.canonicalText.LENGTH. It uses the transcript only for its LENGTH. Nothing in the repository compares u.text to the transcript at u.span; the only two canonicalText references in recall/ are that length check and the segmenter's own construction.

CONSEQUENCE TRACED, which is what makes this load-bearing rather than tidiness: embed-bench/channels.scala:126 embeds u.TEXT - embed(units.map(u => s"unit:${u.id.value}" -> u.text), q) - so the only code in this repo that turns a recall unit into a vector reads TEXT. A span-based trace answers with the TRANSCRIPT AT THAT SPAN. align never sees either; SemanticDistance is an interface and the caller supplies the number. So the semantic term is computed from one string and would be explained by a different one, with no law that they are the same string.

THIS DESTROYS THE PREMISE the joined-trace thread was building on - that returning spans rather than text is the privacy-safe answer. It is privacy-safe and it is NOT FAITHFUL: the words shown would not be the words that produced the number. An explanation that does not correspond to the computation is the estimand disease in a new domain.

NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER TODAY: RecallSegmenter constructs units from the transcript, so on the normal path text and span agree. The divergence needs a hand-built or externally-supplied RecallGraph - which is public API, so a library consumer can build one, and no law refuses it.

CONSTRAINT ON THE FIX, not a prescription - m1 owns the shape: either the two must be provably the same string, or their possible divergence must be TYPED so a consumer cannot mistake one for the other. Do not simply document that they should agree. Note there may be a legitimate reason for both fields (normalization, paraphrase, a recall not drawn from a transcript), in which case the answer is the second option and not the first; establish which before choosing.

FOUND BY claude-storymodel4s-m1, which also checked and DISCARDED a second hypothesis before reporting - that minSpan bounds only the earliest span in a discontinuous SpanSet - by reading core/span.scala:78 and finding minSpan is a hull, so every span is bounded and the check is correct despite the misleading name. It cited its own earlier untraced P1 escalation as the reason it read the definition first.
